methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $7.6B.

private.name: Archer Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $3.33B

data.narrative:
Joby Aviation, a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, is evaluated against a peer set of three same-sector comparables at similar valuation tiers: Zipline (Series G, $7.6B), Nuro (Series G, $6.0B), and Archer Aviation (public, $3.3B). The broader addressable peer universe in this sector includes seven private companies, with Aurora Innovation and Elroy Air among additional reference points.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The three selected comparables yield a median valuation of $6.0B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $7.6B. This method directly anchors to observable market pricing for functionally similar-stage and similarly-capitalized companies in autonomous vehicle and drone technology.

The triangulated valuation range is $5.1B to $6.9B, with a median of $6.0B. Joby's current public valuation of $6.86B falls within the upper bound of this range and sits materially above the peer median. Key uncertainties center on stage-appropriate comparability—Archer Aviation's lower valuation reflects its public-market discount relative to private fundraising rounds—and the heterogeneity of commercial timelines and regulatory pathways across the peer set. The single-method analysis limits confidence; additional triangulation via revenue multiples, DCF, or precedent transaction analysis would strengthen conviction in a specific valuation point.
